policy: Communicative skills are audited against can-do/task evidence, not vocabulary levels.
A broad CEFR descriptor may support a skill family while still requiring LINGUA to define a narrower observable task boundary.
LINGUA_A0 is internal Pre-A1 scaffolding; introducing survival interaction earlier is not an official CEFR A0 assignment.
Skill evidence never changes competence, FSRS, learner status, Save/Learn intent or exposure state.
No skill is production-approved by this audit alone.

sources.name: Council of Europe CEFR Companion Volume
Council of Europe CEFR Global Scale

evidence: CEFR A1 global scale: can introduce self and others and use familiar everyday/basic expressions
CEFR Pre-A1 general linguistic range allows isolated words/basic expressions for simple personal information
records.rationale: A minimal greeting/opening routine is appropriate internal bootstrap before formal A1 interaction. Keep the task narrow and formulaic.

evidence: CEFR Asking for clarification A1: can indicate/express simply that they do not understand
CEFR A2: can ask very simply for repetition and clarification using stock phrases
records.rationale: LINGUA intentionally teaches survival repair phrases before external A1/A2 descriptors. UI/curriculum must label this as internal bootstrap, not CEFR A0 certification.

evidence: CEFR A1 supports following short simple directions
CEFR Obtaining goods/services A2 explicitly supports asking and giving directions
ALTE A1 supports understanding simple directions; A2 supports asking how to get from A to B
records.rationale: The current label conflates A1 location questions ('Where is...?') with A2 route-direction interaction. For A1, narrow to asking a simple location; keep route directions as A2.

evidence: CEFR Obtaining goods/services A1: can ask for food/drink using basic expressions
ALTE A1: can order a meal in a self-service/fast-food setting when supported visually or by pointing
records.rationale: A1 is supported for tightly scoped basic ordering; restaurant discussion/complaints remain later.

evidence: CEFR Obtaining goods/services A2: can point out when something is wrong
CEFR A2: can indicate the nature of a problem to a health professional, perhaps using gesture/body language
records.rationale: A2 supports short concrete problem descriptions in predictable service/travel/health situations.

evidence: CEFR A2 collaborative task interaction: can communicate with simple phrases to discuss what to do next
CEFR B1 expands this to making/responding to suggestions with reasons and reactions
records.rationale: A2 is defensible for one short formulaic suggestion in a familiar task. Suggestions requiring justification, negotiation or comparison belong in B1+.

evidence: CEFR B1 global scale: can briefly give reasons and explanations for opinions and plans
CEFR B1 collaborative interaction: can make opinions/reactions understood regarding possible solutions, giving brief reasons/explanations
records.rationale: The LINGUA skill requires an opinion plus at least one relevant reason, which maps well to B1.

evidence: CEFR B1 spoken interaction: can repeat back part of what someone said to confirm mutual understanding
CEFR B1 Asking for clarification: can ask someone to clarify or elaborate what was just said
records.rationale: B1 is supported for recognizing a routine misunderstanding and actively clarifying/reformulating it; basic non-understanding signalling remains earlier.
